subject: Urgent: New bank details for invoice

findings.title: Potentially executable attachment type
findings.detail: One or more file extensions are commonly used to run code or scripts.
findings.recommendation: Do not run unexpected executable or script attachments.

findings.title: Visible link and destination differ
findings.detail: The domain shown in the link text does not match the clickable destination.
findings.recommendation: Do not trust a link based only on its visible label.

findings.title: Link points to a raw IP address
findings.detail: The URL points directly to an IP address rather than a named domain.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the destination through a trusted website, not this link.

findings.title: Deceptive double-extension filename
findings.detail: A filename appears to disguise an executable/script as a document or image.
findings.recommendation: Check the complete attachment filename and avoid opening disguised files.

findings.title: Unusual payment or bank-details language
findings.detail: Payment changes and fund-transfer requests can signal business email compromise.
findings.recommendation: Verify payment and banking changes using an existing trusted phone number.

findings.title: From and Reply-To domains differ
findings.detail: Replies would go to a different domain than the sender. This can be legitimate, but warrants checking.
findings.recommendation: Contact the organization through a known address instead of replying to this message.

findings.title: Account verification or credential request
findings.detail: A message asks for account verification or secret information.
findings.recommendation: Use the organization's known website or app instead of email links to manage accounts.

findings.title: Submitted header reports authentication failure
findings.detail: Authentication-Results text claims a failure, but the header itself is untrusted and is not independently validated.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat copied authentication headers as verified; confirm suspicious messages separately.

findings.title: Unencrypted HTTP link
findings.detail: The link uses HTTP instead of HTTPS. This alone does not prove maliciousness.
findings.recommendation: Avoid entering credentials or other sensitive details over HTTP.

findings.title: Urgency or pressure language
findings.detail: Pressure can be a phishing tactic, but urgent wording alone is not proof of fraud.
findings.recommendation: Pause before acting on a request that pressures you to respond quickly.

recommendations: Do not open unexpected attachments or follow links until the sender is verified.
Do not run unexpected executable or script attachments.
Do not trust a link based only on its visible label.
Confirm the destination through a trusted website, not this link.
Check the complete attachment filename and avoid opening disguised files.
Verify payment and banking changes using an existing trusted phone number.
Contact the organization through a known address instead of replying to this message.
limitations: Risk scores reflect heuristic indicators and are not proof of safety or maliciousness.
Authentication-Results claims are copied from the submitted email, not independently verified.
URLs are never visited and no live threat-intelligence service is queried.
Attachment files are not executed, extracted, or malware-scanned.
Email content is processed in memory and not stored by default.
